title: SSH Keys and Remote File Transfer
intro: Almost every server you'll ever touch is reached over SSH. Keys instead of passwords, and the right tool for copying files, make this safe and fast.

steps.prompt: Generate a new modern SSH key pair.
steps.fake_output:
Generating public/private ed25519 key pair.
Your identification has been saved in /home/you/.ssh/id_ed25519
Your public key has been saved in /home/you/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
steps.explanation: Creates a private key (never share it) and a .pub public key (safe to put on servers).
steps.why: ed25519 is shorter, faster, and more secure than old RSA-2048 keys. Set a passphrase when prompted — it protects you if the private key file itself is ever stolen.

steps.prompt: Install your public key on the server 10.0.4.20 for user 'deploy', so you can log in without a password.
steps.fake_output:
Number of key(s) added: 1
Now try logging into the machine, with: "ssh 'deploy@10.0.4.20'"
steps.explanation: Appends your public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server, with the correct permissions.
steps.why: Doing this by hand works too, but it's easy to get the permissions on ~/.ssh or authorized_keys wrong — and SSH silently refuses keys from files with overly open permissions.

steps.prompt: Connect to a cloud server using a specific key file, bastion.pem, as user 'ubuntu' at 54.12.34.56.
steps.explanation: -i picks a specific private key instead of your defaults.
steps.why: If this fails with 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE', run 'chmod 600 bastion.pem' — SSH refuses keys that other users could read. When a connection fails for unclear reasons, add -v to see exactly which step breaks.

steps.prompt: Copy a single file, backup.sql, to the server's /tmp directory.
steps.explanation: scp copies over the same SSH connection and keys.
steps.why: scp is fine for a quick one-off file. For anything larger or repeated, rsync (next step) is the better tool.

steps.prompt: Sync your local ./site/ directory to /var/www/site/ on the server, transferring only files that changed.
steps.fake_output:
sending incremental file list
index.html
css/main.css
sent 18,204 bytes  received 92 bytes
total size is 4,812,003  speedup is 263.01
steps.explanation: Only 2 changed files were sent out of ~4.8MB — the 'speedup is 263' is how much less data moved than a full copy.
steps.why: rsync compares files and only sends differences, and can resume. The trailing slash on the source matters: 'site/' copies the contents, 'site' copies the directory itself into the destination — a very common surprise.
